steps.title: C++ Setup and Core Syntax
steps.description: Almost every commercial game engine and its tooling is written in C++, so a working compiler setup and fluent core syntax are the ground everything else in this path stands on. Get a program compiling, then practise types, operators, control flow, functions and pointers until they feel routine.

projects.title: Console number-guessing game
projects.description: A terminal game with a random target, a turn limit and a replay loop, built only from core syntax.

projects.title: Text-mode tic-tac-toe
projects.description: A two-player board game that stores the grid in an array and checks for wins and draws with functions.

videos.title: How to set up C++ in Visual Studio Code

resources.title: Modern Cpp Series By Mike Shah

steps.title: Memory, Ownership and Smart Pointers
steps.description: Games allocate and free thousands of objects every frame, and leaks or dangling pointers are among the most common crash causes in shipped titles. Learn how object lifetime works, why RAII and smart pointers exist, and how undefined behaviour shows up.

projects.title: Leak-hunting exercise
projects.description: Write a small entity spawner with raw new/delete, find its leaks with a tool, then rewrite it with unique_ptr.

projects.title: Resource handle class
projects.description: A RAII wrapper that loads and frees a texture-like resource, following the rule of five.

more_topics.title: SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error)

videos.title: What is RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization)?

Dynamic cast c++ Runtime Type Identification example why we use dynamic cast - RTTI

steps.title: Classes, Polymorphism and the STL
steps.description: Game objects, components and systems are modelled with classes, virtual functions and templates, and the standard containers and algorithms do most of the bookkeeping. This step covers the object model and the parts of the STL you will use daily.

projects.title: Shape and collider hierarchy
projects.description: A base Collider class with circle and box subclasses, stored in a std::vector and tested polymorphically.

projects.title: Templated 2D vector maths
projects.description: A Vec2<T> type with overloaded operators, used to move sprites in a simple simulation loop.

projects.title: Inventory system with STL
projects.description: An item inventory that sorts, filters and searches with containers, lambdas and algorithms.

resource.title: Object Oriented Programming (OOP) in C++ Course

videos.title: Object Oriented Programming (OOP) in C++ Course
Classes part 18 - Understanding the vtable (Popular interview question) | Modern Cpp Series Ep. 54

steps.title: Building, Debugging and Profiling C++ Projects
steps.description: Real game projects span many files and third-party libraries, and performance problems are found with debuggers and profilers, not guesses. Learn how compilation and linking work, manage builds with CMake and packages, and practise debugging and profiling multithreaded code.

projects.title: CMake project with a library
projects.description: Split a small game into headers and source files, build it with CMake and pull one library in through vcpkg.

projects.title: Profile a slow update loop
projects.description: Deliberately write an inefficient particle update, profile it, and measure the speed-up after fixing the hot spot.

resource.title: CMake, How it Works (At Three Different Levels)

videos.title: CMake, How it Works (At Three Different Levels)
What are header files in C++ ( PROGRAMMING TUTORIAL for beginners)
GDB is REALLY easy! Find Bugs in Your Code with Only A Few Commands
vcpkg Crash Course | Visual Studio 2022 | C++ libraries simplified!

steps.title: Game Engines and Their Scripting Languages
steps.description: Studios in India and abroad mostly ship on Unity, Unreal or Godot, and each engine dictates the language you script in. Learn what an engine provides and try one end to end before going deeper into the maths and systems underneath.

projects.title: Same mini-game in two engines
projects.description: Build a one-screen collect-the-coins game in Godot and again in Unity, and note what each engine makes easy.

projects.title: Engine feature comparison sheet
projects.description: Document scene structure, scripting language, build targets and licensing for three engines from hands-on use.

resource.title: Choosing a Game Engine is Easy!

videos.title: Choosing a Game Engine is Easy!

steps.title: Vectors, Matrices and Transformations
steps.description: Every position, direction and camera in a game is a vector or a matrix, so this maths is used on every frame. Work through vectors, matrices and affine and projective transformations until you can place and move objects by hand.

projects.title: Software 3D wireframe viewer
projects.description: Project a rotating cube onto a 2D canvas using your own matrix multiplication and perspective divide.

projects.title: Top-down aiming with vectors
projects.description: A turret that turns to face the mouse using dot and cross products instead of engine helpers.

steps.title: Rotations, Orientation and Curves
steps.description: Cameras, characters and animated paths need smooth rotation and interpolation, and the wrong representation causes gimbal lock and jerky motion. Compare Euler angles with quaternions, then use splines to move objects along curves.

projects.title: Camera rail with Catmull-Rom splines
projects.description: Move a camera smoothly through a set of waypoints and orient it with quaternion slerp.

projects.title: Gimbal-lock demonstration
projects.description: Rotate an object with Euler angles until gimbal lock appears, then fix it with quaternions.

steps.title: Physics: Motion, Forces and Rigid Bodies
steps.description: Believable movement comes from applying forces and integrating velocity every frame, and tuning feel is a core gameplay skill. Learn linear and angular motion, mass properties, friction and restitution, and how joints connect bodies.

projects.title: 2D rigid-body sandbox
projects.description: Simulate boxes and balls with gravity, friction and bounciness using a fixed-timestep integrator.

projects.title: Ragdoll with joints
projects.description: Connect body parts with joints in an engine and tune constraints until the fall looks natural.

resource.title: Playing With Unreal Engine Physics: Center of Mass

videos.title: Playing With Unreal Engine Physics: Center of Mass

steps.title: Collision Detection: Broad and Narrow Phase
steps.description: Checking every object against every other is far too slow for a real scene, so engines first cull candidate pairs and then test them precisely. Learn bounding volumes, spatial partitioning and continuous detection for fast-moving objects.

projects.title: Uniform grid versus brute force
projects.description: Measure pair checks per frame for a thousand moving circles with and without a spatial grid.

projects.title: Bullet tunnelling fix
projects.description: Show a fast projectile passing through a thin wall, then stop it with swept (continuous) collision.

steps.title: Convex Shapes and Collision Algorithms
steps.description: Precise collision between arbitrary shapes relies on convexity, and the separating axis theorem and GJK are the algorithms most engines use. Learn how concave meshes are decomposed into convex pieces and how penetration depth is found.

projects.title: SAT polygon collision demo
projects.description: Detect and resolve overlaps between rotating convex polygons with the separating axis theorem.

projects.title: Convex hull visualiser
projects.description: Compute and draw the convex hull of clicked points, then compare it with the original concave shape.

steps.title: The Graphics Pipeline and Graphics APIs
steps.description: To control what the GPU draws you need to know how vertices become pixels and which API the target platform uses. Study rasterisation and clipping, then compare OpenGL, WebGL, Vulkan and DirectX.

projects.title: Hello triangle in OpenGL
projects.description: Open a window, upload vertex data and draw a coloured triangle with the core-profile pipeline.

projects.title: WebGL sprite renderer
projects.description: A browser renderer that batches textured quads, playable on a phone.

resource.title: How do Video Game Graphics Work?

videos.title: How do Video Game Graphics Work?

steps.title: Shaders, Textures and Materials
steps.description: Shaders decide how every surface looks, and texture and material work is where much of a game's visual identity comes from. Write vertex and fragment shaders and add normal, bump and parallax mapping and specular and metallic responses.

projects.title: Material preview sphere
projects.description: A shader that switches between diffuse, specular and metallic looks with live sliders.

projects.title: Brick wall with parallax mapping
projects.description: Compare flat, bump-mapped and parallax-mapped versions of the same textured wall.

videos.title: Normals, Normal maps and Bump maps

steps.title: Lighting and Shadows
steps.description: Lighting sets the mood of a scene and shadows anchor objects in it, but both are expensive, so games choose their techniques carefully. Implement the main light types and compare shadow mapping, cascaded shadows and stencil shadows.

projects.title: Day-night scene
projects.description: A directional sun with shadow mapping that moves across a small level, plus distance fog.

projects.title: Torch-lit dungeon
projects.description: Point and spot lights with a frame-time budget and a toggle for each shadow technique.

resource.title: How Can We Use Reflection in Game Development?

videos.title: How Can We Use Reflection in Game Development?

steps.title: Visibility, Culling and Advanced Rendering
steps.description: Frame rate depends on not drawing what the player cannot see, and modern titles add physically based shading and ray tracing on top. Learn frustum and occlusion culling, then the rendering equation, PBR and real-time ray tracing APIs.

projects.title: Frustum culling counter
projects.description: Render a large forest and display how many objects are drawn with culling on and off.

projects.title: CPU ray tracer
projects.description: A small ray tracer with spheres, reflections and shadows, written from the rendering equation.

resource.title: Frustum Culling - Game Optimization 101 - Unreal Engine

videos.title: Frustum Culling - Game Optimization 101 - Unreal Engine

steps.title: Game AI: Decision Making and Search
steps.description: Enemies and companions need behaviour that reads as intelligent while staying cheap and predictable for designers. Build state machines and behaviour trees, then use minimax, alpha-beta pruning and Monte Carlo tree search for turn-based games.

projects.title: Guard with a behaviour tree
projects.description: An enemy that patrols, investigates noises and chases the player, built as a behaviour tree.

projects.title: Connect-four opponent
projects.description: A board-game AI using minimax with alpha-beta pruning, compared against an MCTS version.

resource.title: Unreal Engine 5 Tutorial - AI Part 2: Behavior Tree

videos.title: Unreal Engine 5 Tutorial - AI Part 2: Behavior Tree

steps.title: Learning-Based Game AI
steps.description: Machine learning is increasingly used for agents, playtesting bots and content tuning, so knowing where it fits in a game is a useful edge. Survey decision tree learning, Bayesian classifiers, neural networks and reinforcement learning applied to games.

projects.title: Reinforcement-learning racer
projects.description: Train an agent to drive a simple track and compare it with a hand-written waypoint follower.

projects.title: Player-style classifier
projects.description: Classify logged play sessions as aggressive or cautious with a decision tree, then adapt enemy difficulty.
